## About the course

A hands-on introduction to the Linux command line for bioinformatics. The
course handbook works through eight chapters, moving from the shell and
everyday text-processing tools to AWK, Bash scripting and reproducible
software environments, and closing with a pipeline that turns raw biological
data into a report. Each chapter ends with exercises; the final chapter is a
capstone that ties the tools together.

## Topics

1. The Linux command line
2. Overview of command-line tools
3. The VIM text editor
4. Biological data: databases and formats
5. The AWK programming language
6. Bash as a scripting language
7. Software in the Linux environment (Conda, Docker)
8. Writing custom scripts for biological data processing
